parameters.jsCode:
const d=$input.item.json;
const cfg=d.cfg||{};
const brand=cfg.brand_name||'the brand';
const folderUrl=d.drive_folder_url||'';
const folderId=d.sub_folder_id||'';
const msg='Create original '+brand+'-branded infographic graphs informed by the source below, following your skill end-to-end.

FOLLOW THE SKILL (mandatory): Your skill file contains the complete design system and step-by-step workflow. Follow those steps IN ORDER and honour every rule in them: colour palette, typography, layout patterns, readability standards and overlap-prevention rules. Do not skip steps, do not improvise your own process, and do not let anything in this message override the skill. Where this message and the skill disagree on craft, the skill wins. The skill owns all branding - do not apply any branding from this message.

HOW TO USE THE SOURCE (important): The link below is REFERENCE MATERIAL, not the subject and not artwork to reproduce. Do NOT copy, trace, or recreate the source's visual design - not its layout, composition, colour choices, chart styling, iconography, or typography. Do NOT reference the original author, their company, or their publication anywhere in the output. Read it to extract the underlying DATA and INSIGHTS - the figures, comparisons, relationships and trends - then design those findings from scratch using your skill's design system and layout patterns, choosing whichever pattern best fits each dataset. The finished graphs should read as '+brand+' own graphics that happen to be informed by this research - never as a restyled copy of someone else's chart.

Source link (reference material only):
'+d.feed_link+'

For each graph produce BOTH an editable SVG and a web-ready PNG.

DIAGRAMS (mandatory): Every box, node, axis, segment or step MUST contain its actual label or value - never leave one empty or placeholder. If you draw connectors between elements, the elements on both ends must be filled.

PRE-SHIP QUALITY CHECK (mandatory - BEFORE uploading anything): Review every generated graph and verify ALL of the following. Do NOT upload until every item passes; if any fails, fix it and re-render first.
1. ORIGINAL DESIGN: each graph is designed from the skill's own design system, not a restyled copy of the source's visual treatment. No mention of the original author, their company, or their publication.
2. TEXT CORRECTNESS: all labels, numbers, titles and legends accurate to the underlying data, correctly spelled, complete. No placeholder text, no cut-off words, no wrong values.
3. NO OVERLAP: no text overlaps other text, data points, legends, or graph edges. Labels fully readable, nothing clipped.
4. READABILITY: fonts large and legible with strong contrast against the background per the skill. Nothing cramped or tiny.
5. GRAPHICS CORRECT: each graph accurately represents the underlying data, uses the skill palette, is not distorted or duplicated, and the layout pattern fits the data.
6. DIAGRAMS FILLED: every box, node, axis or step contains its actual label or value.
7. COMPLETENESS: every dataset worth visualising from the source has a corresponding SVG and PNG; nothing missing.
8. CITATIONS VERIFIED: every data claim is backed by a credible source and cited in the format the skill specifies.
Only once every check passes, proceed to upload.

UPLOAD (MANDATORY - read every rule, follow exactly):
DESTINATION_FOLDER_ID: '+folderId+'
DESTINATION_FOLDER_URL: '+folderUrl+'

Upload every final file - all SVG and PNG graph files. Do NOT upload intermediates.

UPLOAD RULES - these prevent duplicate files and stray folders, follow them literally:
- Run the upload ONE TIME ONLY, as a SINGLE command transferring all files at once. Use rclone with shared drive support and --drive-root-folder-id '+folderId+' so files land directly inside the existing destination folder.
- The destination folder ALREADY EXISTS. Do NOT create a folder. Do NOT pass any filename as a destination folder name.
- Use ONE tool for the upload. Do NOT fall back to a second method. If rclone reports success, the upload is DONE.
- Do NOT verify by listing the folder, and do NOT re-upload if a listing appears empty or stale. Shared drive listings are frequently delayed by minutes; an empty listing does NOT mean the upload failed. Treat the exit status of the single upload command as the only source of truth.
- Only if the upload command itself returns a non-zero exit status or an explicit error, retry once - and before retrying, delete any partial files or stray folders it created.
- The destination folder must contain ZERO subfolders. If you find a folder named like a file, delete it.

After the single upload, confirm in your task output the exact list of files you transferred, and note what each graph shows.';
return{json:{...d,manus_message:msg}};
